narrative: During the 2010s, Black and African women's hairstyles and hair culture flourished as part of a broader movement towards self-expression and identity. The natural hair movement gained momentum, with women embracing their textured hair in its inherent state without chemical relaxers or heat-straightening. Hairstyles like afros, cornrows, and dreadlocks became popular, celebrating the diversity of African textures and kinks. Protective styles, such as box braids and Bantu knots, were also favored for their ability to minimize manipulation and exposure to environmental elements, promoting hair health and self-care. These hairstyles not only reflected individual identity but also connected women to their cultural heritage and community, serving as a powerful expression of Black and African femininity. While the source material does not provide extensive documentation on this decade specifically, it offers valuable insights into the hairstyling practices and cultural significance that defined this era for many Black and African women.
